statement: A preserved branch is never proven and its author is told the wrong thing. Since the non-main preservation fast path landed (79e8c7cb9 + 4c98b0a59) a push of only non-main branch refs skips the local gate, and ci.yml runs only on pushes to main and pull requests into main, so quest/, land/ and review/ branches (and the stacked PRs whose heads they are) carried reds nobody saw; ci.yml also still carries a dead '[ci:self-hosted]' commit-message route to a label only the offline GCP proof VM has, with a header claiming pull requests can never reach a self-hosted runner, which a pull request's own copy of the workflow can always do. Owner decisions 2026-10-04 (after the rejected preserved-branches-get-their-cone, which this supersedes; its findings and measurements stand by reference): D1 a push to quest/**, land/** or review/** runs ci.yml's change gate on a GitHub-hosted runner, proving the CONE of the pushed head against its merge-base with main (not before..after, not HEAD^), never the corpus: a cone the selector refuses fails the run by name (MODULAR PROOF NOT SAFE) exactly as for a pull request, and nothing the branch run reaches is a corpus entry point or main's structural analysis; a newer push to the same branch cancels the superseded run, while main's runs are never cancelled; main pushes and pull requests into main run the same steps against the same base as before; permissions stay contents: read. D2 wip/** and every other prefix stay free of CI. D3 the '[ci:self-hosted]' route is retired: ci.yml has no trigger, label or expression by which any event selects a runner other than a GitHub-hosted one (no pull_request_target), the resource plan names the literal hosted label, publish refuses --runner as a retired option with a clear message, action-authority no longer registers route-self-hosted-runner, and no tracked file outside quest history names the marker. D4 the pre-push fast path keeps exactly one line: for a push whose pushed branches a workflow's push trigger covers it names that workflow (ci.yml for the three prefixes, full-gate.yml for release-proof/**, release.yml for release-publishability/**); otherwise it says the push is unproven unless an open pull request into main covers it and gives the cone command with its precondition, from a clean checkout at <sha> (the first uncovered commit; with a count when several refs are uncovered); nothing for a main push, LAGRANGE_PUSH_PROVE_BRANCH or a deletion-only push; the hook's prefix list is bound by a witness to the prefixes derived from every workflow's parsed push trigger, and the runbook states the command's prerequisites (exact clean checkout, generated import graph).

constraints.statement: No workflow or script file is added; existing files change; net workflow lines do not grow; ratchet baselines only tighten; the apparatus budget metric does not get worse.
No trigger of ci.yml reaches the whole corpus on a hosted runner; a refused cone fails, it is never widened.
The steps, base and cancellation of main pushes and pull requests into main are those of d60c30921.
Which refs a workflow proves is the workflows' push triggers; the hook's list is a mirror bound by a witness, and the runner of every job is the resource plan's literal.
